title: The patent doesn't.
description:
The patent doesn't. Yokoi ran the division that shipped it. He isn't the name on the paperwork.

Nintendo's cross-shaped pad first shipped inside the Game & Watch version of Donkey Kong, credited on the eventual patent to Shirai rather than his better-known boss.

Nintendo filed for it in August 1985 and wasn't granted it until August 1987. Five years after the D-pad had already shipped to shops.

Filed the actual first cross-style four-way controller patent, for Tiger Electronics, it shipped on Tiger's 1980 football handheld as the 'Playmaker' button, two years before Nintendo's version existed.

Not the cross shape, a smaller pad, built for the left thumb, using membrane switches instead of Palisek's bulkier domed ones. That's the whole distinguishing claim, in writing.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D-pad: read. Establishes that Nintendo's cross-shaped D-pad was 'developed by Ichiro Shirai' and first used in the 1982 Game & Watch adaptation of Donkey Kong; that its patented distinguishing features over the earlier Tiger Electronics design were being smaller, positioned for the left thumb, and using membrane switches instead of domed ones; that William F. Palisek patented 'the first true D-pad design for Tiger Electronics' in 1979, debuting on Tiger's 1980 Deluxe Football with Instant Replay handheld as the 'Playmaker' button; and that Nintendo later won a Technology & Engineering Emmy for the design.
- https://patents.google.com/patent/US4687200A/en: read (primary
- https://patents.google.com/patent/US4256931A/en: read (primary). Confirms US4256931A, 'Multiple dome switch assembly having pivotable common actuator,' inventor William F. Palisek, original assignee Interstate Industries Inc (current assignee Tiger Electronics Toys Inc), filed and granted-priority 1979-08-27, published 1981-03-17.
